source.title: CA3 retrieves coherent representations from degraded input: direct evidence for CA3 pattern completion and dentate gyrus pattern separation

confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available empirical demonstration that separation and completion are performed by DIFFERENT STAGES on the SAME input, and it is the key entry for the SD-016 H2 (structured retrieval unit) leg rather than for H3. Its methodological strength is the simultaneity: recording DG and CA3 at once during a local-global cue conflict removes the usual confound of comparing separately-recorded populations under nominally-matched conditions, and it lets the authors show DG input to CA3 was severely disrupted WHILE CA3's own output stayed coherent. That is a within-animal, within-session dissociation, which is a much harder result to explain away than the region-by-region comparisons that preceded it. Confidence is held below the Espinoza entry for two reasons: the mapping to SD-016 is architectural-by-analogy (REE has no DG/CA3 stage separation to map onto, so the paper motivates BUILDING one rather than validating an existing design), and the double-rotation cue-conflict paradigm is a specific spatial-navigation manipulation whose relationship to REE's safe-vs-dangerous context distinction requires an inferential step the paper does not license directly.
failure_signatures: Separation and completion are ANTAGONISTIC operations, and the paper's framing is that CA3 arbitrates between them. A single-stage selection mechanism (SD-016's current design) has no place to put that arbitration and may be structurally incapable of achieving both -- pushing toward separation degrades retrieval of a stored association from a partial cue, and pushing toward completion collapses distinct contexts together. The uniform-selection saddle may be what 'maximum completion / zero separation' looks like from the outside.

CA3's behaviour depends on the RELATIVE STRENGTH of its internal attractor dynamics against its external inputs (Knierim & Neunuebel 2016 make this explicit). A retrieval unit with no recurrent/attractor component has no internal dynamics to weigh against input, so the separation-completion balance is not a parameter it possesses -- it is fixed implicitly by the architecture.

DG's pattern separation in this study is expressed via changes in FIRING RATE of place-modulated granule cells rather than by recruiting non-overlapping cell populations; Leutgeb et al. 2007 found the population-recruitment mechanism in CA3 but not DG. A REE design that assumes 'separation == disjoint slot selection' imports only one of the two biological mechanisms and may miss rate-coded separation entirely.

The result is obtained in a cue-CONFLICT paradigm (local and global reference frames placed in opposition), which is an unusually strong perturbation. It does not establish that the same separation/completion division operates under ordinary, non-conflicting input.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Simultaneous recordings from DG and CA3 in behaving rats during a local-global cue conflict (double rotation) show that the two regions respond differently to the same perturbation. DG's representation of the conflict changed MORE than its entorhinal inputs did (pattern separation), while CA3's representation changed LESS than its entorhinal and DG inputs did (pattern completion / error correction). CA3 thus produced an output pattern closer to the originally stored representation than the degraded input patterns it received from DG, confirming the hallmark predictions of long-standing computational models of hippocampal memory.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-016 currently asks one feedforward stage to do the whole job: take z_world, and select which of 16 ContextMemory slots is relevant. This paper says the biological system does not do it in one stage, and that the two stages perform OPPOSITE transformations -- DG amplifies input differences, CA3 suppresses them in service of retrieving a stored pattern. That is the core motivation for the H2 (representation) leg of the GOV-FANOUT-1 portfolio: the question is not only which operator selects (H3) but what UNIT is being selected over, and whether a single stage that must simultaneously separate contexts and retrieve stable content is being asked to satisfy two conflicting objectives at once. Read that way, the uniform-selection saddle acquires a candidate interpretation the autopsy did not have: uniform mixing over all 16 slots IS maximal pattern completion with zero pattern separation -- the degenerate corner of the separation-completion trade-off, which is exactly what a stage with no separation pressure and a retrieval objective would be expected to settle into. That reframing is testable and is the most useful thing this entry contributes.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The mapping is architectural-by-analogy and motivates a build rather than validating one: REE has no DG/CA3 stage separation for this result to map onto, so the paper argues for CREATING a two-stage structure rather than confirming the current one. Three specific gaps. (i) The separation/completion dissociation is measured over SPATIAL representations under a cue-conflict manipulation; SD-016's contexts are safe-vs-dangerous terrain, and the claim that these are the same kind of distinction is an inferential step this paper does not license. (ii) CA3's completion depends on recurrent attractor dynamics, which SD-016's feedforward tagger does not have and which would be a substantial (not minimal) build. (iii) The suggested reinterpretation of the ln(16) saddle as 'the completion corner of the trade-off' is MY inference from this result, not a finding of the paper, and should be treated as a hypothesis to test rather than as evidence -- specifically, it predicts that adding separation pressure should move entropy and context-divergence together, which the H3 leg will incidentally test.
mapping.source_context: Simultaneous single-unit recordings from DG and CA3 in freely-behaving male Long-Evans rats; local-global cue-mismatch (double-rotation) paradigm on a circular track.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron, Knierim lab; the simultaneous DG+CA3 recording during cue conflict is the methodological advance that makes this the canonical direct evidence for the separation/completion division of labour, and it is widely cited as such. Source quality 0.88. Mapping fidelity 0.70 because REE has no two-stage retrieval architecture for this to map onto -- the entry motivates the H2 build rather than grounding an existing mechanism, and one of its most useful contributions (the saddle-as-completion-corner reading) is my inference rather than the paper's finding. Transfer risk 0.35: spatial cue-conflict in rats to safe/dangerous terrain contexts in an artificial agent is a real domain jump, mitigated by the fact that the imported content is a computational division of labour rather than a spatial result.
